texts.preamble: Shellz Overseas Pvt. Ltd vs Food Safety Officer on 23 September, 2020 In The Court Of Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma Principal District & Sessions Judge / Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No. 18/2019 1. Shellz Overseas Pvt. Ltd. 39/35, 3rd Floor, Main Rohtak Road, Near Shivaji Park Metro Station, West Punjabi Bagh, New Delhi26 2. Tifosi Foods Pvt. Ltd. 99, Main Chowk, Samaypur, Delhi42 ..... Appellants Versus Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place, New Delhi01 .....Respondent Date of filing of appeals : 14.05.2019 Date of arguments : 15.09.2020 Date of judgment : 23.09.2020 Fsat No. 18/2019 Page 1 of 6 Judgment
texts.facts: The allegations in brief are that on 02.11.2015, Sh. Ranjeet Singh, Food Safety Officer (FSO) had taken a sample of "Sugar Based Confectionery", an article of food for analysis from Sh. Sushil Kumar S/o Sh. Madan Lal, Food Business Operatorcum Proprietor, M/s Sharma, Confectionery, Shop No. 1, Rai Singh Market, Karari Road, Sultanpuri, Delhi110 086, where the said food article was found stored for sale for human consumption at the time of taking the sample. The food article was available in the sealed packets having identical lable declaration upon them. 3. The sample was sent for analysis. The Food Analyst vide his report No. FSS/992/2015 dated 07.11.2015 reported that the sample was found misbranded because there was violation of Regulation No. 2.2.1.3 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulations, 2011. Upon inquiry, it was found that the food article was supplied by appellant M/s Shellz Overseas Pvt. Ltd. and manufactured by M/s Tifosi Foods Pvt. Ltd. 4. The report of the Food Analyst was sent to the FBO/Supplier/Manufacturer but they did not prefer any appeal against it. 5. Ld. Adjudicating Officer after analyzing the case and hearing the parties, imposed a penalty of Rs.2,40,000/ in the ratio of 60% upon the manufacturer company, 30% upon the supplier company and 10% on FBO. It is pertinent to mention here that the FBO did not file any appeal against it. 6. In appeal, the appellants have assailed the impugned order on the ground that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer has passed the order in a routine manner without taking into account all the facts and circumstances of the case. 7. Notice was issued to the respondent. The respondent has contested the appeal and submitted that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer has passed a reasoned order after taking all the submissions of the parties and there is no illegality or impropriety therein. 8. The sample was also brought in the Court and was perused as under: "On opening one of the brown paper/sheet, it is found containing one original sealed box of "Hugs Silky Premium Rich Cocoa Bar". It has been observed during physical inspection of the case property being produced by the Designated Officer Sh.S.P.Singh that "Sugar Based Confectionery & Mfg.: SEP.2015" is printed at the side of the sealed box." 9. During the course of submission, Ld. Counsel for the appellants submitted that he only wishes to challenge the order of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer to the extent of minimizing the penalty.
texts.arguments: It has been submitted that a lenient view may be taken and the penalty amount may be reduced. (1) Any person who whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption which is misbranded, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to three lakh rupees. (2) The Adjudicating Officer may issue a direction to the person found guilty of an offence under this section, for taking corrective action to rectify the mistake or such article of food shall be destroyed." 13.
